correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<a<b,d>0, z-y=d and lambda=b-a, the exact change V=by/(ax),W=bd/(lambda x),d tau/dt=x gives classical LV equations V_tau=lambda V(1-W),W_tau=aW(V-1), and physical dt/dtau=(lambda/(bd))W. H=a f(V)+lambda f(W) has compact regular positive levels. Each inverse branch V=v_±(q_h(W)) supplies original-time density B_h(W)=1/(1-v_-)+1/(v_+-1). Near branch endpoints B-1=O(q^-1/2), in the bulk its excess is O(1/q)+exponentially small. The w-variable change has controlled Jacobian outside [1/2,2] and bounded middle error, proving I_h=h/lambda+O(log h) and T(h)=h/(abd)+O(log h). Thus lambda W/h approaches U(0,1) in total variation at O(log h/h); its reciprocal hX/(bd)=1/U approaches Pareto(1,1) in TV with same bound. The high-V branch has O(log h/h) physical mass and typical low-V branch V→0, so state→(0,0,d) in probability; integrating periodic log derivatives proves positive exact means bd/lambda,ad/lambda,bd/lambda. Independent check: Performed independent symbolic differentiation of V and W from the displayed mass-action system: both transformed derivative differences simplify identically to zero. Rechecked the endpoint inverse f(s)=s-1-log s derivative bounds, rescaled interval length, and exact normalization w*/(a lambda)=1/(abd). Prior finite-energy quadrature in source verification is supplemental only.
residual_risks: Strictly positive chemical class z-y=d, fixed 0<a<b and d>0; no uniformity as a→b or d→0, no stochastic population law.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Banaji–Boros–Hofbauer already prove the lifted center and time-change; Boulnois treats period-energy asymptotics of the classical LV clock. The published same-week dual occupation law analyzes classical LV ordinary and reaction-flux weighted times and a different variable normalization; it does not imply the present exact hX/(bd) Pareto TV bound without additional clock and inverse-branch estimates.
